public_rationale: Marcus predicts eventual improvement without a deadline or a defined success threshold. The records show promising hybrid developments: graph-enhanced retrieval improves results in one study, and AWS offers formal checks against domain policies. These are material evidence in the forecast's direction. They do not establish the independently corroborated, broader reliability advantage required by this interpretation. Separate fact-validation research also finds inconsistent benefits from retrieval and consensus. No decisive event meets the early-resolution rule, and the passage of time cannot falsify 'eventually'.
limitations: The result depends on how broadly 'something better' is read.
The graph study covers one benchmark and one model and was funded by Neo4j.
AWS's announcement is provider evidence, not independent validation.
Context items establish progress and limitations; none settles the forecast.

statement.document_title: Why DO large language models hallucinate?

from_speaker: We will eventually get to something better

our_interpretation: In context, 'better' means materially better factual reliability and checking of answers against records or sources.
A qualifying approach moves beyond reliance on an LLM alone. A hybrid using language models alongside databases or symbolic verification can qualify.

I require reproducible comparative evidence across varied factual tasks, with independent corroboration, to establish a successor's reliable advantage. These evidence requirements are mine, not thresholds Marcus supplied.
Neither widespread adoption nor complete elimination of hallucinations is required by his words.
The criticism of investment choices is evaluative rhetoric and is not part of the forecast being scored.
criteria.support_condition: A post-publication non-LLM or hybrid approach demonstrates a reproducible, independently corroborated improvement in factual accuracy and source verification over the LLM approach discussed, across varied factual tasks and without obtaining its advantage merely by declining more questions.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Decisive evidence rules out the predicted improvement. Failure to produce a qualifying successor by any finite evaluation date does not contradict 'eventually'.
